title: Liver and Onions
subtitle: Calves' liver with slowly caramelised onions and a mustardy pan sauce
excerpt: Liver and onions is a British pub classic: thinly sliced calves' liver cooked quickly in a pan, served with onions that have been cooked slowly in butter until golden and sweet. The liver must cook fast or it will turn grainy. The onions must cook slowly or they will be sharp. These two things cannot be rushed.
sourceNotes: Liver and onions in the style of calves' liver with caramelised onions was popularised in British cooking by Elizabeth David and other mid-twentieth-century writers as a Venetian-influenced dish (fegato alla veneziana). It overlaps with older British offal traditions where liver was an economical and nutritious cut.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the caramelised onions up to 3 days ahead and refrigerate. Reheat gently while cooking the liver.

glossaryTerms.definition: To add liquid (stock, wine, or water) to a hot pan after frying, loosening the browned residue to form a quick sauce.

content.text: Liver and onions is a dish that rewards confidence. The calves' liver goes into a very hot pan and comes out 2 minutes later: that is all it can take. The onions are the opposite: they need 25 to 30 minutes over low heat to reach the soft, golden sweetness that makes them worth eating. Do the onions first, keep them warm, and the liver takes 4 minutes from start to plate.

Melt {{unsalted-butter}} of butter in a heavy pan over low heat. Add {{onion}} finely sliced onions and the sage if using. Cook for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deep golden and sweet. Season with salt and pepper and keep warm.
Dust {{calves-liver}} of liver slices in {{plain-flour}} of flour, shaking off the excess. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat {{unsalted-butter}} of butter in a separate frying pan over high heat until foaming and just starting to colour. Add the liver slices in a single layer. Cook for 1 minute per side only: the liver should be just faintly pink in the centre. Lift out immediately and rest on a warm plate for 3 minutes.
With the pan still hot, pour in {{stock-beef}} of beef stock and stir to
the pan. Add {{wholegrain-mustard}} of wholegrain mustard and bubble for 1 minute. Season and pour over the liver. Serve with the caramelised onions alongside.

items.symptom: The liver is grainy and tough
items.cause: It was cooked too long or over low heat.
items.fix: Liver must go into a very hot pan and come out after 1 minute per side. Anything beyond 2 minutes total and it will be tough. It finishes cooking during the rest.

items.symptom: The onions are bitter rather than sweet
items.cause: The heat was too high and the onions browned rather than caramelised.
items.fix: Caramelise over the lowest heat that will maintain a gentle sizzle, with occasional stirring. Brown onions taste sharp; caramelised onions taste sweet.

items.symptom: The liver is metallic in flavour
items.cause: Calves' liver can have an edge when it is not properly rested.
items.fix: Rest the liver for 3 full minutes after cooking. The resting allows the temperature to equalize and the flavour to settle.

items.cause: The stock did not reduce enough in the pan.
items.fix: Let the stock bubble for a full minute before adding the mustard. If still too thin, reduce for another minute.

content.text: Liver and onions is old-fashioned and unfashionable in some quarters, but it is one of those dishes that becomes remarkable when it is done right. Calves' liver is milder than ox or pig liver. It cooks very fast, which leaves little room for error. Get the heat right and the timing right, and the result is hard to argue with.
